significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that "the vector of acquired-trait strengths across the bank is a susceptibility fingerprint" that quantitatively predicts base ancestry across fine-tuning, quantization, and distillation—a form-(iii) predictive coupling rather than merely an existence or single-behavior causal claim. It would fix the expectation that derivatives remain preferentially susceptible to lineage-matched hidden signals and establish a weighty behavioral phenomenon and provenance regularity, although it would not by itself prove the proposed internal explanation in terms of "shared base geometry." Cloud et al.'s subliminal-learning results make base-model matching a load-bearing premise; a negative result here would meaningfully show that this specificity is not stable or discriminative enough across derivative transformations for lineage attribution, without refuting subliminal learning itself. Topic substitution fails: merely restating "extend research on subliminal learning" would not license the specific lineage-prediction conclusion, so the score is above the topic median.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "susceptibility fingerprint," a measurable vector of acquired-trait strengths usable as a lineage-classification and clustering diagnostic. It is post hoc with respect to the model's ancestry, but it can operate before procurement or deployment decisions and is explicitly positioned for "AI supply-chain auditing," giving auditors rather than only subliminal-learning researchers a practical action window. After per-model probing, the claimed relation predicts high susceptibility to same-lineage references and near-zero susceptibility to others; thus the substantive prediction, not just a search procedure, is asserted to transfer across "closed, fine-tuned, quantized, or distilled" derivatives, subject to short fine-tuning access. Topic substitution again fails because subliminal learning in general supplies neither this provenance handle nor its asserted cross-transformation relation.
